title: Asthma
qa: What does a silent chest mean? Severe obstruction; life-threatening.
How can exercise-induced symptoms be reduced? Warm-up, prescribed pre-exercise reliever, avoid cold dry air.
Why check inhaler technique? Poor technique is a common cause of poor control.
What is dysfunctional breathing? An abnormal breathing pattern (upper chest, rapid, sighing) causing symptoms, sometimes alongside asthma.
When is PEF useful? Tracking variability and recognising deterioration against the personal best.

redFlags.Finding: Unable to complete sentences, RR above about 25, HR above about 110, PEF 33 to 50% of best
redFlags.Action: Reliever as per action plan, emergency services [Ref – to verify BTS criteria]

redFlags.Finding: Silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, confusion, PEF below 33%

manualNotes: Breathing retraining (for example Buteyko-informed or physiotherapy-led programs): nasal breathing, slower and lower breathing, relaxation; improves symptoms and quality of life in some patients [Ref – to verify]. Exercise: aerobic training improves fitness and may improve control. Warm up gradually for 10 to 15 minutes, use interval or low-to-moderate continuous efforts, avoid cold dry air or use a mask, cool down slowly. Education: inhaler technique with spacer, action plan, trigger avoidance.
